questions.stem:
Which of the following contain the same number of atoms ?
(Given : Molar mass in $\mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$ of H, He, O and S are 1, 4, 16 and 32 respectively).
A. $2\ \mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{O_2}$ gas
B. $4\ \mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ gas
C. $1400\ \mathrm{mL}$ of $\mathrm{O_2}$ at STP
D. $0.05\ \mathrm{L}$ of He at STP
E. $0.0625\ \mathrm{mol}$ of $\mathrm{H_2}$ gas
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
$n_{\mathrm{O_2}} = \frac{2}{32}$
No. of atom (O) $= 2 \times \frac{2}{32} \times N_A = 0.125 N_A$
$n_{\mathrm{SO_2}} = \frac{4}{64}$
No. of atom $= 3 \times \frac{4}{64} \times N_A = 0.1875 N_A$
$n_{\mathrm{O_2}} = \frac{1400}{22400}$
No. of atom $= \frac{1400}{22400} \times 2 \times N_A = 0.125 N_A$
$n_{\mathrm{He}} = \frac{0.05}{22.4}$
No. of atom $= \frac{0.05}{22.4} \times N_A = 0.0022 N_A$
$n_{\mathrm{H_2}} = 0.0625$
No. of atom $= 0.0625 \times 2 \times N_A = 0.125 N_A$

questions.stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
Given $V_1$ and $V_2$ are initial and final volumes respectively.
List-I (Isothermal process) | List-II (Expression)
A. Reversible expansion | I. $q = 0$
B. Free expansion | II. $q = nRT\ln\frac{V_2}{V_1}$
C. Irreversible Compression | III. $w = -p_{ext}(V_1 - V_2)$
D. Cyclic reversible | IV. $\frac{q_{rev}}{T} = 0$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Isothermal process
Reversible expansion $\Delta U = 0$
$w = -q$
So, $q = -w = -\left(-nRT\ln\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$
$= nRT\ln\frac{V_2}{V_1}$
$A \rightarrow II$
Free expansion
$q = 0$
$B \rightarrow I$
Irreversible compression
$W = -p_{ext}(V_2 - V_1)$
Cyclic reversible
$\frac{q_{rev}}{T} = 0$
$D \rightarrow 4$

(Given $R = 0.083\ \mathrm{dm^{3}\ bar\ K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}}$ and assume complete dissociation of electrolyte)
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Chamber I: 18 g glucose, 100 mL | SPM | Chamber 2: 30 g glucose, 250 mL
Molarity chamber 1 $= \frac{18/180}{100/1000} = 1$
Molarity chamber 2 $= \frac{30/180}{250/1000} = 0.67$
$\mathrm{H_2O}$ molecules will move from chamber 2 to chamber 1.
So, statement 1 is false.
$\pi = iCRT$ ($\mathrm{K_2SO_4}$, $i = 3$)
$= 3 \times \frac{\frac{50 \times 10^{-3}}{174}}{2} \times 0.083 \times 300$
$= 0.0107\ \mathrm{bar}$
So, statement II is true.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.stem: Given is a concentrated solution of a weak electrolyte $\mathrm{A_xB_y}$ of concentration 'c' and dissociation constant 'K'. The degree of dissociation is given by :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{A_xB_y \rightleftharpoons xA^{y+} + yB^{x-}}$
$c$
$c - \alpha \qquad xc\alpha \qquad yc\alpha$
$k = \frac{(xc\alpha)^{x}(yc\alpha)^{y}}{c - c\alpha}$
$k = \frac{x^{x}y^{y}c^{x+y-1}\alpha^{x+y}}{1 - \alpha}$
$1 - \alpha \simeq 1$
$\alpha = \left(\frac{k}{x^{x}y^{y}c^{x+y-1}}\right)^{\frac{1}{x+y}}$

questions.stem:
For a general redox reaction
Anode: $\mathrm{Red_1 \rightarrow Ox_1^{n_1+} + n_1e^{-}}$
Cathode: $\mathrm{Ox_2 + n_2e^{-} \rightarrow Red_2^{n_2-}}$
Which of the following statement is incorrect ?
questions.solution:
Anode: $\mathrm{Red_1 \rightarrow Ox_1^{n_1+} + n_1e^{-}}$ $\times n_2$
Cathode: $\mathrm{Ox_2 + n_2e^{-} \rightarrow Red_2^{n_2-}}$ $\times n_1$
$\mathrm{n_2red_1 + n_1Ox_2 \rightarrow n_2Ox_1^{n_1+} + n_1Red_2^{n_2-}}$
Statement I is correct.
The $e^{-}$s do not appear in the overall reaction.
Statement II is correct.
$\Delta G = \Delta G^\circ + RT\ln Q$
$-nFE = -nFE^\circ + RT\,2.303\log Q$
$E = E^\circ - \frac{RT\,2.303}{nF}\log Q$
$E - E^\circ = -\frac{RT\,2.303}{nF}\log Q$
$\frac{E - E^\circ}{\frac{RT}{F}} = -\frac{2.303}{n}\log Q$
slope $= -\frac{2.303}{n}$
Statement III is correct.
$\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ =$ electrical w done
$nF =$ charge
$E^\circ =$ potential difference
Statement IV is incorrect.

options.text: The overall reaction can be written as $\mathrm{n_2\,Red_1 + n_1Ox_2 \rightleftharpoons n_2Ox_1^{n_1+} + n_1\,Red_2^{n_2-}}$
The electrons do not appear in the overall reaction because electrons produced at the anode are consumed at the cathode.
[Graph: $\frac{(E - E^\circ)}{RT/F}$ vs $\log_{10}Q$ for $n = 1, 2, 3$; Slope $\propto \frac{1}{n}$] Here n is the number of electrons transferred in redox reaction.
If the reaction is carried out reversibly, the electrical work done is equal to the ratio of charge and potential difference through which charge is moved.

questions.solution:
$\mathrm{CH_3-C(=O)-\ddot{O}-CH_3 \longleftrightarrow CH_3-C(-O^{-})=O^{+}-CH_3}$

questions.stem:
In a closed flask at $600\ \mathrm{K}$, one mole of $\mathrm{X_2Y_4(g)}$ attains equilibrium as given below :
$\mathrm{X_2Y_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2XY_2(g)}$
At equilibrium, 75% $\mathrm{X_2Y_4(g)}$ was dissociated and the total pressure is $1\ \mathrm{atm}$. The magnitude of $\Delta_rG^\ominus$ (in $\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$) at this temperature is ______. (Nearest Integer)
(Given : $R = 8.3\ \mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}\ K^{-1}}$; $\ln 10 = 2.3$, $\log 2 = 0.3$, $\log 3 = 0.48$, $\log 5 = 0.69$, $\log 7 = 0.84$)
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{X_2Y_4 \rightleftharpoons 2XY_2}$
$P$
$P - P\alpha \qquad 2P\alpha$
$P - P\alpha + 2P\alpha = P_T$
$P_T = \frac{P}{1 + \alpha}$
$K_P = \frac{(2P\alpha)^{2}}{P(1 - \alpha)}$
$= \frac{4P\alpha^{2}}{1 - \alpha} \qquad \alpha = 0.75$
$= \frac{4P_T\alpha^{2}}{1 - \alpha^{2}}$
$= 5.14$
$\Delta G^\circ = -RT\ln K_P$
$= -8153.99$
$\simeq -8154$
$\simeq -8.154\ \mathrm{kJ/mole}$
